That divides <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-4.6</annotation></semantics></math> by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>25</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25</annotation></semantics></math>. After eliminating <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> the equation is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>15</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">15a = -4.6</annotation></semantics></math>, so divide by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">15</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: A student solves a system for a model's constants, rounds <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>0.31</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.31</annotation></semantics></math>, and then uses that value to find <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math>. Why is this a problem?
options: Rounded values lose their negative sign

The rounding error carries into <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> and every prediction made with the model
The system has no solution once <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> is rounded
Calculators do not accept decimals in a system

items.q: Evaluate <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>8</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8^{2/3}</annotation></semantics></math> without a calculator.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>8</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8^2</annotation></semantics></math>. The <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math> in the denominator takes a cube root: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mroot><mn>8</mn><mn>3</mn></mroot><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\sqrt[3]{8})^2</annotation></semantics></math>.

That multiplies <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2}{3}</annotation></semantics></math>. A fractional exponent is a root and a power, not a product.

items.q: Simplify <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x^3)^2 \cdot x^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math> to a single power of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: A power of a power multiplies the exponents: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(x^3)^2 = x^6</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>5</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^5</annotation></semantics></math>.

Multiplying powers with the same base adds the exponents: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6 + (-4) = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

Add the exponents of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>6</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^6 \cdot x^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>; do not multiply them.

items.q: What is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{-3}</annotation></semantics></math>?

Evaluate <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>16</mn><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16^{-1/2}</annotation></semantics></math> exactly.

mistakes.why: The negative exponent gives a reciprocal, not a negative number: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{4}</annotation></semantics></math>.

This multiplies <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">16</annotation></semantics></math> by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. The exponent <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> is a square root.

items.q: Write <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{x^3}</annotation></semantics></math> as a power of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, for <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>></mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x > 0</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: The root goes in the denominator: a square root of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^3</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x^{3/2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

A root of a power multiplies the exponents: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3 \cdot \frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Simplify <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>3</mn></msup><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2x^3)^2</annotation></semantics></math>.

Solve <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4^x = 32</annotation></semantics></math> by writing both sides as powers of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That divides <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">32</annotation></semantics></math> by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>. Rewrite with a common base and compare exponents.

That is the exponent of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>; the left side is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{2x}</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x = 5</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Which expressions equal <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>9</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{9}</annotation></semantics></math>? Select all that apply.

A student writes <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>7</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^3 \cdot 2^4 = 4^7</annotation></semantics></math>. What is the error?
options: The exponents should be multiplied, giving <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>12</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{12}</annotation></semantics></math>

The base stays <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>; only the exponents are added, giving <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>7</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^7</annotation></semantics></math>
The bases should be added, giving <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mn>12</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4^{12}</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: A right triangle has legs of length <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">15</annotation></semantics></math> and hypotenuse <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>17</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">17</annotation></semantics></math>. The angle <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> is across from the leg of length <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math>. What is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin B</annotation></semantics></math>?

In the same triangle (legs <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">15</annotation></semantics></math>, hypotenuse <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>17</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">17</annotation></semantics></math>), the other acute angle is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math>, across from the leg of length <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">15</annotation></semantics></math>. What is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan C</annotation></semantics></math>?

mistakes.why: That is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan B</annotation></semantics></math>. From <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> the opposite side is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">15</annotation></semantics></math> and the adjacent side is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math>: the legs swap names.

That is opposite over hypotenuse, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>C</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin C</annotation></semantics></math>. Tangent is opposite over adjacent.

items.q: A 10-foot ladder leans against a wall. Its foot is 6 feet from the wall on level ground. Let <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> be the angle between the ladder and the ground. What is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan\theta</annotation></semantics></math>?

A kite string 40 meters long makes an angle of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>55</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">55^\circ</annotation></semantics></math> with the level ground. Use <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mn>55</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup><mo>≈</mo><mn>0.8192</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin 55^\circ \approx 0.8192</annotation></semantics></math> to find the kite's height above the hand holding the string, in meters.

mistakes.why: That divides 40 by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.8192</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.8192</annotation></semantics></math>. The height is opposite the angle and the string is the hypotenuse, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>40</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mn>55</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h = 40 \sin 55^\circ</annotation></semantics></math>: multiply.

That divides <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>0.8192</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.8192</annotation></semantics></math> by 40. From <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mn>55</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>h</mi><mn>40</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin 55^\circ = \frac{h}{40}</annotation></semantics></math>, multiply both sides by 40.

items.q: A right triangle has hypotenuse <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math> and an acute angle <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>. Write the length of the side adjacent to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> in terms of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Sine goes with the opposite side. The adjacent side uses cosine: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mtext>adjacent</mtext><mn>8</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\theta = \frac{\text{adjacent}}{8}</annotation></semantics></math>.

From <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mtext>adjacent</mtext><mn>8</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\theta = \frac{\text{adjacent}}{8}</annotation></semantics></math>, multiply by 8; do not divide.

The unknown is on top of the ratio, so multiply: adjacent <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 8\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: In a right triangle, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>5</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin A = \frac{3}{5}</annotation></semantics></math> for the acute angle <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math>. What is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos A</annotation></semantics></math>?

Right triangle 2 is right triangle 1 with every side multiplied by 3. Both have an acute angle of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>40</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">40^\circ</annotation></semantics></math>. How does <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mn>40</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin 40^\circ</annotation></semantics></math> found from triangle 2 compare with <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mn>40</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin 40^\circ</annotation></semantics></math> found from triangle 1?
options: It is one third as large

items.q: A wheelchair ramp rises 2 feet over a horizontal distance of 24 feet. Let <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> be the angle the ramp makes with the ground. What is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan\theta</annotation></semantics></math>?

mistakes.why: That is run over rise. Tangent is opposite over adjacent: rise <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> over run <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>24</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">24</annotation></semantics></math>.

That multiplies the sides. Tangent is a ratio: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>2</mn><mn>24</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{2}{24}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: From a point 30 meters from the base of a tree, on level ground, the angle up to the top of the tree is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>50</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50^\circ</annotation></semantics></math>. Use <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mn>50</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup><mo>≈</mo><mn>1.192</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan 50^\circ \approx 1.192</annotation></semantics></math> to find the height of the tree, in meters.

mistakes.why: That divides 30 by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1.192</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.192</annotation></semantics></math>. The height is opposite the angle and 30 is adjacent: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mn>50</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>h</mi><mn>30</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan 50^\circ = \frac{h}{30}</annotation></semantics></math>, so multiply.

That adds the ratio to the distance. Multiply: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mn>50</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h = 30 \tan 50^\circ</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: A right triangle has an acute angle <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\theta = 0.6</annotation></semantics></math> and adjacent side 9. Put the steps for finding the hypotenuse <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> in order.
options: Name the sides from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>θ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math>: 9 is adjacent, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> is the hypotenuse

Choose the ratio that links them: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mi>x</mi></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos\theta = \frac{9}{x}</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: A 45-45-90 triangle has legs of length <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6</annotation></semantics></math>. What is the exact length of its hypotenuse?

mistakes.why: That adds the legs. The hypotenuse is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mrow><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{6^2 + 6^2} = 6\sqrt{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, shorter than the two legs together.

That divides the leg by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{2}</annotation></semantics></math>. The hypotenuse is the longest side: multiply, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>6</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6\sqrt{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: A 30-60-90 triangle has hypotenuse <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10</annotation></semantics></math>. What is the exact length of the leg across from the <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>60</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60^\circ</annotation></semantics></math> angle?

mistakes.why: That is the short leg, across from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>30</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">30^\circ</annotation></semantics></math>. The leg across from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>60</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">60^\circ</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mn>3</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{3}</annotation></semantics></math> times the short leg.

That scales the long leg by 10, but the hypotenuse is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> in the basic triangle, so the scale factor is 5.

items.q: What is the exact value of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mn>60</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sin 60^\circ</annotation></semantics></math>?

What is the exact value of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mn>45</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\cos 45^\circ</annotation></semantics></math>?

mistakes.why: That is hypotenuse over leg, upside down. Cosine is adjacent over hypotenuse: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>tan</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><msup><mn>45</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tan 45^\circ</annotation></semantics></math>, leg over leg. Cosine divides by the hypotenuse <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: A circle has radius 9 cm. What is the exact length, in centimeters, of the arc cut off by a central angle of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>80</mn><mo>∘</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">80^\circ</annotation></semantics></math>?

mistakes.why: That uses the diameter 18 in place of the radius. The circumference is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>18</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi r = 18\pi</annotation></semantics></math>; take <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>80</mn><mn>360</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{80}{360}</annotation></semantics></math> of it.

That multiplies the angle by the radius. The arc is a fraction of the circumference: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>80</mn><mn>360</mn></mfrac><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{80}{360} \cdot 2\pi(9)</annotation></semantics></math>.
